newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee dips on late demand for dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee dips on late demand for dlrs.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed lower on late commercial demand for dollars, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.74 to the dollar, after opening at 57.64. The rupee closed at 57.70 on Monday, the last trading day.
"The rupee opened at 57.64, but banks quoted two-way rates with no trading taking place, until some commercila demand emerged in the afternoon, said a Union Bank dealer.
The exchange rate finally moved between 57.71-57.78, he said.
Overnight call money closed at 13 percent, after moving between 12.5 and 14 percent, dealers said.
"The money market is very liquid, and no one sees a real reason for rates to climb," said the Union bank dealer.
Treasury Bill yields fell again at Wednesday's auction, with three-month, six-month and one-year rates easing 0.37 percentage points, 0.22 and 0.21, respectively.
